- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Logitech G502 is a popular choice with a 12,000 CPI optical sensor, customizable buttons, and RGB lighting, priced at $99.99.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The SteelSeries Rival 600 features a 12,000 CPI TrueMove3 optical sensor, customizable weight system, and is priced at $99.99.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Corsair M65 RGB Ultra Wireless has a 15,000 CPI optical sensor, customizable RGB lighting, and is priced at $99.99.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The HyperX Pulsefire Raid features a 16,000 CPI Pixart 3389 sensor, customizable RGB lighting, and is priced at $99.99.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Logitech G502 has 11 programmable buttons, including a sniper button, and uses Logitech Gaming Software (LGS) for programming.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The SteelSeries Rival 600 has 6 programmable buttons and uses SteelSeries Engine software for programming.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Both mice have user-friendly software for programming buttons and creating custom profiles.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] CPI stands for Counts Per Inch, measuring mouse sensitivity and accuracy.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] A lower CPI setting (400-800) is suitable for precise movements, while a higher CPI setting (3200-12000) is suitable for fast, aggressive gameplay.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] For Apex Legends, a higher CPI can be beneficial for fast-paced gameplay, but it depends on the user's playstyle.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Suggested CPI ranges for different playstyles in Apex Legends: 2400-3200 for aggressive players, 1600-2400 for medium-range engagements
